question: Which article of the constitution of India lays down the uniform civil code?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 44**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 44** is part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy.**
 
• It urges the** state to strive for a Uniform Civil Code for all citizens, regardless of their religion.**
 
• This would mean a common set of laws governing personal matters like **marriage, divorce, inheritance, etc., for all citizens.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 377: **
 
• **This article** does not exist in** the Indian Constitution.**
 
• However, **Section 377** of the Indian Penal Code was a colonial-era law that criminalized homosexual acts, which was decriminalized by the **Supreme Court of India in 2018.**
 
• **Article 370: **
 
• This article gave special autonomous status to the state of **Jammu and Kashmir,** allowing it to have its constitution,** flag, and autonomy** over internal administration.
 
• However, in August 2019, the Indian government abrogated most provisions of **Article 370.**
 
• **Article 12: **
 
• This article is part of the** Fundamental Rights in Part III of the Indian Constitution.**
 
• It provides the definition of the **State **and the authorities against whom **Fundamental Rights** can be enforced.
